title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues from the previous one. X is a topological space, near x a surface, and U = X minus the marked points. D_x^* is the 'residual germ' of X at x, i.e. the punctured-neighbourhood germ. [I] is the residual germ of I=[0,1] at 0, i.e. the germ of ]0,ε]; it is 1-connected. A 'germ of arc of curve from x' is a morphism of germs γ:[I]→D_x^*. Concretely, it is a continuous φ:[0,ε]→X with φ(0)=x and φ(t)≠x for t>0. Because [I] is 1-connected, Rev([I]) ≅ (Ens), so γ gives a fibre functor on Rev(D_x^*) (eq. 69). Since x is a surface point, Rev(D_x^*) is Galois cyclic with group T_x, which is Z, or Ẑ in the profinite version.

This page.
(70) The arc-pointed fibre functor defines a universal covering D_x^{*~} = Rev univ(D_x^*, ([I],φ)), a pro-object or germ of covering.
Because [I] is 1-connected, the arc lifts canonically: [I]→D_x^{*~}→D_x^*↪U, with composite φ.
(71) Hence universal coverings of U pointed by the 1-connected germ D_x^{*~} are canonically the same as those pointed by the arc [I]→U.
(second '71', i.e. 72) Therefore π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) = π_1(U,[I]), and there is a canonical homomorphism K_x: T_x → π_1(U,[I]). This is the local inertia or monodromy map. It is now defined on the nose, not up to conjugacy, because the base point is a germ of path issuing from the puncture.

So the page is the topological construction of what are now called tangential base points (or 'base points at a puncture'). Using a germ of path from x as base point makes the inertia subgroup a well-defined subgroup, not a conjugacy class. This is what is needed for the Galois action on π_1 of P^1 minus points, curves and moduli in the Longue Marche programme.

Section D starts relating this to differentiable structure. If X is differentiable near x, a germ of arc is differentiable if a representative I→X is differentiable and its tangent map R→Tang_x(X) at 0 is injective (completed on the next page). The image of R^+ is then a half-line, the 'demi-tangente'. The intended link is that the arc-germ base points up to homotopy are governed by tangent half-directions, i.e. the circle of directions in T_xX. This is the bridge to algebraic tangential base points (tangent vectors at a puncture).

The next page organises all arc germs into the 'local fundamental groupoid' Chemins(X,x). Its morphisms are the isomorphisms of the pointed universal coverings, and it is equivalent to Revêtements(D^*); it is a connected groupoid with vertex group T_x.
errors: Equation number (71) is used twice. The second one (π_1 equality with the K_x arrow) should be (72), consistent with (73) on the next page.

No real mathematical error. Implicitly the 'universal covering' of a germ D_x^* must be read as a pro-object or germ of covering, and the factorization through D_x^{*~} uses the 1-connectedness of [I]. Both points are standard but left tacit.
K_x need not be injective in general, e.g. when U is a disc or the plane minus a point. The page does not claim injectivity, so this is only a caution.

ideas.what: Using a germ of arc issuing from a puncture x as a base point (fibre functor) for coverings of the punctured germ D_x^* and of U, giving a canonical lift into the universal cover.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point / base point at a puncture (topological version); paths from the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points' (1989), §15; also Ihara and Nakamura in the 1990s; Kato–Nakayama log-topological version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses base points and Teichmüller groupoids for the Galois action; this explicit arc-germ construction appears unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Canonical inertia homomorphism K_x: T_x → π_1(U,[I]) defined on the nose (not up to conjugation) thanks to the arc base point.
ideas.modern_name: inertia / local monodromy at a tangential base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989; Ihara; folklore in anabelian geometry

ideas.what: Differentiable arc germs with injective tangent map determine a half-tangent (ray) in T_xX, linking topological arc base points to tangent directions.
ideas.modern_name: tangent directions as base points; circle of directions / real oriented blow-up boundary; tangential base points given by tangent vectors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (algebraic tangent vectors); A'Campo / real oriented blow-up; Kato–Nakayama

ideas.what: The local fundamental groupoid at x whose objects are arc germs from x (next page), equivalent to the groupoid of pointed universal coverings of D_x^*.
ideas.modern_name: local fundamental groupoid at a puncture (groupoid with tangential base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; tangential-base-point groupoids in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura)

missed.claim: This is a pre-Deligne (Longue Marche period, c. 1981) topological construction of tangential base points via germs of arcs. It is set up explicitly to make the inertia map T_x→π_1(U,[I]) canonical, and is followed by a passage to half-tangents under a differentiable structure. It documents Grothendieck's own priority on the idea of base points at punctures, which the literature attributes to Deligne (1989).
missed.quote: π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) = π_1(U,[I]) ←^{K_x}— T_x ; D) Relation avec structure différentiable ... demi-tangente
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is history-of-ideas credit for tangential base points in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. Mathematically the content is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is correct and is exactly the topological counterpart of tangential base points. Its interest is mainly priority and documentation: it is Grothendieck's own early formulation, apparently unpublished, of what is credited to Deligne/Ihara. There is no new mathematics beyond what specialists know.
transcription_corrections: 'où I est considéré comme un germe 1-[?] sur U' — likely reads 'un germe 1-connexe sur U' (or possibly '1-pointé'); the following words are 'par le morphisme composé'.
'donc [?] un iso can' — likely 'd'où aussi un iso can' or 'donc un iso can'.
The second equation labelled '(71)' in the manuscript should be (72).

Sentence order in section D: '...si le germe d'application continue I → X qui le définit est différentiable, et de plus [next page:] l'application tangente à l'origine ... est injective' — the 'et de plus' belongs after 'différentiable', not before 'qui le définit'.
Margin heading reads 'D) Relation avec structure différentiable' (written diagonally).
